note: Shared INPUT for the EPIC-12 GPX writer parity fixture. Both suites build their own GPXWorkout/GPxWorkout objects from this file, run their own GPXWriter/GpxWriter, and must produce route_<id>.gpx byte for byte (goldens in this folder). Read by apps/ios/Tests/GPXAggregationParityTests.swift and apps/android/app/src/test/java/net/albayyan/badan/GpxAggregationParityTest.kt. Numbers are strings so both platforms parse them through Double(String)/String.toDouble() — the correctly-rounded parse — instead of a bare JSON literal each platform's decoder interprets its own way (same reasoning as packages/fixtures/export/README.md 'Why the numbers are strings'). Timestamps are epoch-millis strings.

coverage.01JQZ8WKATRN00000000000001: one route, five points: a 60s gap that must NOT split (boundary is strictly >60s) then a 61s gap that must, and a point with no elevation so <ele> is conditionally emitted
coverage.01JQZ8WKACTY00000000000002: two routes → a route-boundary segment split even though timestamps continue; southern/western (negative) coordinates; a dyadic-rational latitude (25 + 1/256 = 25.00390625) that %.7f rounds differently on the two platforms' printf implementations but integer-space rounding renders identically; a near-zero negative longitude that must keep its sign; a negative (below-sea-level) elevation
